newsitem.title: USA: Tropical Storm Bill expected to bypass Bermuda.
newsitem.headline: Tropical Storm Bill expected to bypass Bermuda.

text.p: Tropical Storm Bill picked up speed and strength as it raced through the Atlantic on Friday and was expected to pass north of Bermuda, hurricane forecasters said.
At 5 p.m. EDT (2100 GMT), Bill, the second named storm of the 1997 Atlantic season, was located at latitude 33.6 north, longitude 67.3 west, about 185 miles (295 km) west-northwest of Bermuda.

It was moving to the northeast near 21 mph (34 kph) and was expected to continue on that track for at least 24 hours, taking the centre of the storm away from Bermuda late on Friday, the National Hurricane Centre said.
A tropical storm warning was in effect for Bermuda but forecasters expected to discontinue it later on Friday.
Maximum winds increased from 45 mph (72 kph) to 50 mph (80 kph) on Friday afternoon.
Tropical depressions become tropical storms and are given names when maximum winds reach 39 mph (62 kph). Hurricanes form when winds top 74 mph (118 kph).
The first tropical storm of the season, Ana, formed on July 1 off the North Carolina coast but bypassed Bermuda and faded as it moved northeast in the Atlantic without touching land.
